To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

'Catalyst Clemente, a collaborative model of higher education, has the potential to increase social inclusion and social capital for people with multiple disadvantage.' The research has shown that the Catalyst Clemente model has been effective in supporting people with multiple disadvantage to access and complete higher education, and to improve social capital, social inclusion and social connectedness.

Catalyst Clemente is: a collaborative model of education that provides a supportive learning environment for students with multiple disadvantage, that is embedded in community, that is cost effective and that is a model of good practice for social inclusion.

Catalyst Clemente has: * a positive and significant impact on participants' lives, including their social inclusion and well-being, and on their communities; * an impact on participants' educational outcomes and on the way in which they are perceived and treated by others; * the potential to be scaled up, and the potential to be replicated in other settings; and * an impact on the way in not-for-profit organisations and universities work together.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How do we understand and measure social inclusion? What does it mean to be socially included? How do we understand the relationship between social inclusion, education and employment? What is the impact of social inclusion on individuals and communities? What does it take to be socially included and what are the barriers to being socially included?
the social inclusion of people experiencing multiple disadvantage through higher education.
the question of how to create a model of university education for vulnerable Australians that is both community-embedded and socially-supported.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Catalyst Clemente has been successful in its objectives to provide a model of university education for people experiencing multiple disadvantage.
• The Catalyst Clemente model is an effective model for enabling access to and participation in higher education for Australians who have experienced multiple disadvantage.
Catalyst Clemente is effective in supporting social inclusion and that the collaborative model is effective in supporting the social inclusion of Australians who experience multiple disadvantage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Catalyst Clemente is about creating a community of learning and support that enables students to achieve their goals and aspirations.
Catalyst Clemente is an innovative and effective approach to social inclusion through education.
the Catalyst Clemente program is a successful and cost effective model of university education.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are all responsible for the social exclusion of others and we are all responsible to be part of the solution.
the Catalyst Clemente model is a powerful vehicle for social inclusion.
people experiencing multiple disadvantage have a right to higher education and the benefits of this.
